answer: The protocol implements a vine of zero-knowledge reputation commitments anchored to a verifiable delay beacon to ensure agents remain tethered to unique cryptographic identities. By enforcing an exponential cost function relative to stake density, an attacker attempting a Sybil meadow suffers strictly negative expected utility and prohibitive capital lockup. This equilibrium forces rational agents to prioritize long-term BFT consensus participation over malicious replication, maintaining protocol stability.
